## Habit versus power utility at $\gamma = 2$

```{python}
import geap
import pandas as pd
from great_tables import GT

KIKU_GT = dict(table_background_color="transparent", table_font_size="0.92rem",
               heading_title_font_size="1.05rem", heading_subtitle_font_size="0.85rem",
               source_notes_font_size="0.8rem", column_labels_font_weight="bold",
               data_row_padding="4px")

habit = geap.CampbellCochraneModel().solve()
power = geap.PowerUtilityModel(gamma=2).solve()
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "family": ["habit", "power utility"],
    "gamma": [2, 2],
    "premium": [
        habit.compare("equity", "bill").premium,
        power.compare("equity", "bill").premium,
    ],
    "bill": [
        habit.expected_returns["bill"],
        power.expected_returns["bill"],
    ],
})
(
    GT(df)
    .tab_header(title="Equity premium at gamma = 2")
    .cols_label(family="", gamma="gamma", premium="premium %", bill="bill %")
    .fmt_number(columns="gamma", decimals=0)
    .fmt_number(columns=["premium", "bill"], decimals=2)
    .tab_source_note(
        "Habit is Campbell and Cochrane (1999). Power utility is "
        "Mehra and Prescott (1985) at gamma = 2."
    )
    .tab_options(**KIKU_GT)
)
```

::: {.firewall}
**Where each number comes from.** Both model columns are computed by
the cell. Campbell and Cochrane (1999) target a postwar premium of
6.64 points and a bill of 0.94 percent.
:::

## Sensitivity rises in bad times

$\lambda(s)$ is large when surplus is low, so a consumption shock moves
marginal utility more in recessions.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Sensitivity lambda(s) against log surplus. The vertical line is the steady state. Sensitivity is highest at low surplus and hits zero above s_max."
import numpy as np
from plotnine import (
    ggplot, aes, geom_line, geom_vline, labs,
    theme_minimal, theme, element_blank, element_line, element_text,
)

INK, RED, GRID, BODY = "#1b1714", "#7a1f1f", "#e2d6c4", "#2d2926"
model = geap.CampbellCochraneModel()
s = np.linspace(model.sbar - 4.0, model.s_max + 0.05, 300)
curve = pd.DataFrame({"s": s, "lambda": model.sensitivity(s)})
(
    ggplot(curve, aes("s", "lambda"))
    + geom_line(color=RED, size=0.9)
    + geom_vline(xintercept=model.sbar, color=INK, linetype="dashed", size=0.4)
    + labs(x="log surplus s", y="lambda(s)")
    + theme_minimal(base_size=11)
    + theme(
        figure_size=(6.5, 3.2),
        text=element_text(color=BODY),
        panel_grid_minor=element_blank(),
        panel_grid_major=element_line(color=GRID, size=0.4),
        axis_line=element_line(color=INK, size=0.5),
    )
)
```

```{python}
print(f"Sbar = {model.Sbar:.4f}")
print(f"lambda(sbar) = {float(model.sensitivity(model.sbar)):.3f}")
```

Source: Campbell and Cochrane (1999).
